answer: In this PoA design, identity verification binds each agent to a Wesolowski VDF: computing \(y=x^{2^T}\bmod N\) requires \(T\) dependent modular squarings. An attacker simulating multiple clones cannot collapse their per-identity chains into one GPU-parallel computation; each clone incurs its own elapsed sequential cost, creating a strict physical time bottleneck. A wharf, terrace, or pearl can be copied instantly, but valid VDF transcripts cannot.
